newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - Stringent test for world champ athletes.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - Stringent test for world champ athletes.

text.p: WELLINGTON, April 16 - Members of the New Zealand team named for the world track and field championships will have to pass stringent new fitness tests to confirm their places, NZPA reports.
Athletics New Zealand's fitness criteria will come into play for the first time for the event in Athens from August 1 to 10.
Fitness criteria were introduced following a disappointing showing at last year's Atlanta Olympics, where half of New Zealand's athletes failed to perform to their potential.
Twenty-one athletes have been provisionally named by selectors for the world championships.
The athletes have all satisfied Athletics NZ selectors that they have achieved International Amateur Athletics Federations (IAAF) A or B qualifying standards within the time period.
However, they will need to demonstrate their fitness by passing individually prepared tests two weeks before leaving for the July pre-championship tour.
Athletes will again have to prove their competitiveness in the final fortnight before competition by attaining a pre-determined standard, most likely a B qualifying time or distance.

Convener of selectors Dave Norris said that in making the selections provisional, Athletics NZ was giving a clear indication to qualifiers that they would be at the championships providing their competitive fitness was satisfactory.
"However, it also sets up a system to ensure that those carrying injuries or poor form will not be going," he said today.
New Zealand athletes named today for the world athletics championships in Athens:

A 4 x 100m relay team to include Nketia and Donaldson plus four of: Mathew Coad (Wellington), Nick Cowan (Palmerston North), Donald MacDonald (Wellington), Paul Gibbons (Auckland), Mark Keddell (Canterbury), Dean Wise (Waikato).
